finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") and discards the boolean result. It then runs purgeAll() for any caller, so the admin check is never enforced.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (or any request that has a User in context) sent to the purge route, with no admin permission.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) takes the caller's User from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the return value is ignored and there is no if/return

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm only returns a bool and writes no 403 itself. There is no other check in the handler. The sibling rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure, which shows the intended pattern. Only handlers.go exists in the directory, so routing and middleware could not be inspected. Whether the route is wrapped in an upstream admin guard is unknown, but nothing in the code shown enforces it.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no upstream middleware is present in the directory)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, discarding its bool (defined at handlers.go:12-14, no abort or 403), so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33. Any upstream route guard could not be checked because only handlers.go exists.
